sentences.text: Researchers developed a brain-on-chip model containing human stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons in a central channel, flanked by specific microglial cells in side channels, to examine the effects of a chemical that induces Parkinson's-like symptoms in mice.
The health and electrical activity of these neurons were monitored using microelectrode arrays, which track signals such as firing rates and synchronization.

While direct exposure of the dopamine neurons to the toxic chemical significantly reduced their spontaneous electrical activity, exposing only the microglial cells did not cause a significant change in the nearby neurons' activity.
The authors suggest that this chip system, which allows real-time recording of neurons with or without microglia, is a promising tool for studying Parkinson's disease and other brain conditions.
